Acadian growth model benchmarking

FVS-ACD version evolution, regional validation, and model comparison · 29 June 2026 · CRSF / University of Maine

Contents
1. Objectives · 2. Models tested · 3. Growth-model bias (version evolution, regional) · 4. What drives the bias (increment vs mortality) · 5. Long-term projections (Bakuzis) · 6. FVS-ACD vs OSM · 7. FVS-NE · 8. Bottom line

1. Objectives

Following the AcdBenchCompare framework, this report evaluates the evolution of FVS-ACD toward a new production version on two axes: (1) the bias of predictions against observed remeasurement growth, across model versions and regions; and (2) the biological reasonableness of long-term projections, including a head-to-head against the Open Stand Model (OSM). Percent bias is reported as predicted over observed minus one, so a positive value is an FVS-ACD over-prediction. The production candidate is AcadianGY 12.6.1 (see the production version spec).

3. Growth-model bias

3.1 Version evolution (NB / NS / ME regional, 5 to 7 yr)

Each version at its native released configuration on 270 regional remeasurement plots. All-region percent bias:

versionBAstems (TPA)QMDsawlog MBFvalue $
12.5.0+6.8+6.8+1.1+7.2+8.0
12.6.0+3.3+3.9+0.8+3.6+4.2
12.6.1+3.3+3.9+0.8+3.5+4.1

The 12.6.0 self-thinning roughly halves the over-prediction across every component; 12.6.1 holds it (ingrowth is near-invisible at the 5 to 7 year horizon because recruits have not reached merchantable size). Extending back, the pre-v12 v9.6 over-predicts basal area by +17% on the Seven Islands CFI (long-horizon +23 to +25%), so the long arc is a monotone reduction in over-prediction from v9.6 to the candidate.

3.2 Regional bias of the candidate (12.6.1), by region

regionBAstemsQMDvalue $
all (270)+3.3+3.9+0.8+4.1
Nova Scotia+5.1+6.7+0.1+4.5
New Brunswick-2.8-1.8-0.5-4.3
Maine+11.1+10.0+2.9+13.3

Bias is regionally heterogeneous: Maine over-predicts most, New Brunswick under-predicts. This is a regional-calibration signal, not a uniform offset.

4. What drives the bias: a regional mortality deficit, not a growth excess

A tree-level decomposition on 15,020 matched pairs compared predicted and observed diameter increment. The result overturns the earlier inference that the over-prediction is a growth problem: in Maine the increment under-predicts (-14.5%) while basal area and stems over-predict, which can only mean too few stems die. The regional basal-area bias is therefore driven by the regional mortality parameters, not the diameter increment. The increment separately shows a size-form bias (over-grows small, under-grows large) and under-prediction at high density.

5. Long-term projection reasonableness (Bakuzis)

On 150-year site-gradient projections, the candidate passes Eichhorn (volume a site-independent function of height, CV 5.1%) and height monotonicity. The self-thinning slope improves from -1.08 to -1.24 with the SDImax-ceiling mortality (target -1.605). Two flags are informative: the height site-curves are nearly coincident (the current site variable barely separates productivity classes, the motivation for the refined ESI), and continuous ingrowth makes stem count non-monotone.

6. FVS-ACD versus OSM (model-vs-model, long-term)

OSM v2.26.1 and FVS-ACD 12.6.1 were projected forward from the same Seven Islands starting inventories (9 matched stands). They start matched (basal area about 31 m2/ha) and diverge sharply: OSM accumulates to a ~40 m2/ha plateau while FVS-ACD self-thins and declines to ~25 by age 80, a ~60% divergence, with OSM growing larger trees (QMD 22 vs 19).

There is no observed 80-year endpoint to adjudicate, but the divergence is first-order for yield and carbon projection and is driven by FVS-ACD's high-density growth suppression and self-thinning; the likely-correct trajectory sits between the two.

7. FVS-NE

FVS-NE is the compiled Fortran variant and cannot be run in the AcadianGY R harness, so its column is not reproduced here. The model documentation records that the FVS-ACD Kuehne increment equations are substantially more conservative than FVS-NE (which over-predicts in the Acadian region). To complete this column quantitatively, use the existing AcdBenchCompare FVS-NE runs.

8. Bottom line for the production decision

12.6.0 and 12.6.1 measurably improve on 12.5.0 (regional over-prediction halved) and on the pre-v12 line, and are safe drop-ins on operational stands. The candidate is 12.6.1. The remaining first-order issue is regional mortality calibration (the Maine deficit), which together with the refined ESI is the agenda for the next production version. Long-horizon projections carry real model-form uncertainty, bracketed here by the OSM comparison.
